# Contributing Guide — Kntro-Soft / wawa-fuerte

Thanks for contributing to **Wawa Fuerte**, the offline Flutter app that generates weekly
nutrition plans against childhood anemia with **Gemma running on-device**. This guide describes the
workflow the team follows to keep the repository organized, the history clean, and the build green.

This is a **6-hour sprint** for _Build with Gemma: GDG Callao_. The priority is a demo that runs on a
real phone, not architectural purity — but the rules below are cheap and they are what keep four
people merging into one working build.

## Prerequisites

- **Flutter** (stable channel) with **Dart 3**
- **Android SDK** + a **physical Android phone** with USB debugging enabled — Android is the primary
  target ([ADR-0003](../docs/adr/0003-android-as-primary-target.md))
- **Lefthook** (optional but recommended) for the pre-commit formatting hook
- Access to the `Kntro-Soft/wawa-fuerte` repository

On macOS, Xcode and the iOS Simulator replace the Android SDK for **non-inference work only** (UI,
RAG, nutrition, storage). The simulator is CPU-only with a 256 MB Metal cap and **cannot run the
model**, so anything touching inference must be validated on a physical Android handset before it is
called done.

## Local Setup

```bash
# 1. Clone and install Dart/Flutter dependencies.
git clone https://github.com/Kntro-Soft/wawa-fuerte.git
cd wawa-fuerte
flutter pub get

# 2. Verify your toolchain and that a device is attached.
flutter doctor
flutter devices

# 3. (Optional) install the pre-commit formatting hook.
lefthook install
```

**The Gemma model is not in the repository.** The quantized `.task` checkpoint weighs over 1 GB and
`assets/models/` is git-ignored ([ADR-0004](../docs/adr/0004-flutter-gemma-over-mediapipe.md)). Get
it from a teammate over USB or file transfer and drop it in `assets/models/`. A fresh clone runs
fine without it — it falls back to `FakeInferenceService`, which returns a hardcoded plan.

**There is no backend and there are no API keys.** The app is 100% on-device
([ADR-0002](../docs/adr/0002-no-backend-on-device-only.md)). If your change appears to need a network
call or a secret, something was designed wrong — raise it with the team before writing it.

## Run, Format and Test

```bash
flutter run                        # run on the attached device
flutter run -d <device-id>         # pick a device when several are attached
dart format .                      # format all Dart sources
dart format --set-exit-if-changed .  # verify formatting (same check CI runs)
flutter analyze                    # static analysis
flutter test                       # unit and widget tests
flutter build apk --debug          # produce an installable APK for the demo phone
```

CI runs `flutter pub get`, `dart format --set-exit-if-changed .`, `flutter analyze` and
`flutter test` on every pull request and on pushes to `main` and `develop`. All four must pass.

**Formatting workflow:** the Lefthook pre-commit hook runs `dart format` on staged `.dart` files and
re-stages them. `flutter analyze` is deliberately **not** in the hook — it takes 10–30 s and that is
minutes lost per commit across four developers, so it lives in CI. If you bypass hooks
(`--no-verify`), run `dart format .` manually before pushing or CI will reject the branch.

**Testing:** favour fast unit tests on the pieces where correctness is not negotiable — the iron
requirement tables and coverage arithmetic in `core/nutrition/`, the retrieval ranking in
`core/rag/`, and the storage schema in `core/storage/`. Iron totals are computed in Dart, never
generated by the model ([ADR-0005](../docs/adr/0005-rag-instead-of-fine-tuning.md)), so they are
ordinary arithmetic and must be tested as such. Widget tests run against `FakeInferenceService`;
never write a test that requires the real model.

**Hemoglobin is nullable everywhere** ([ADR-0007](../docs/adr/0007-hemoglobin-is-always-optional.md)).
No code may assume it is present, and no flow may block on it. Every consumer of the child profile
needs a test covering the `null` case.

## Project Structure

```
lib/
  core/
    inference/   # Gemma + MediaPipe via flutter_gemma.   OWNER: P1
    rag/         # recipe retrieval over the INS corpus.  OWNER: P2
    nutrition/   # iron requirement and coverage math.    OWNER: P2
    storage/     # local SQLite/Hive persistence.         OWNER: P4
    theme/       # colors, typography.                    OWNER: P3
  features/
    onboarding/  # child profile capture.                 OWNER: P3
    home/        # child selector.                        OWNER: P3
    plan/        # weekly plan generation and detail.     OWNER: P3
  main.dart                                             # OWNER: P1
assets/
  data/          # recetario_ins.json and friends.        OWNER: P4
  models/        # Gemma .task (git-ignored, >1 GB)
```

Ownership is enforced socially, not mechanically — see [`CODEOWNERS`](./CODEOWNERS).

### Conventions

- **Do not edit another owner's folder.** If your change crosses a boundary, ask in the team chat
  first. This is the main source of merge pain with four people in one repo.
- **Only P1 edits `pubspec.yaml` and `main.dart`.** Need a package? Ask. `pubspec.yaml` is the
  number-one merge-conflict source in a Flutter team.
- **Never commit the model.** `assets/models/` is git-ignored for a reason; a 1 GB blob makes every
  clone unusable.
- **Copy the nearest existing screen** before creating a new one — folder layout, naming, widget
  shape. Consistency beats elegance when the code has to merge in four hours.
- **Inference goes through the `InferenceService` interface**, never directly against
  `flutter_gemma`. The seam is what lets the app degrade to a canned plan instead of to nothing.
- **State management** follows the single reference implementation written by the `core` owner; see
  [ADR-0009](../docs/adr/0009-state-management.md). Do not introduce a second idiom.
- **`main` always compiles.** A PR that breaks startup is reverted, not debugged on `main`.

When this guide and the code disagree, **the code wins** — update this guide. When this guide and an
ADR disagree, **the ADR wins** ([docs/adr/](../docs/adr/)).

## Branch Structure

We follow **Gitflow** ([ADR-0008](../docs/adr/0008-gitflow-branching.md)):

| Branch                  | Purpose                                                                   |
|-------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `main`                  | Release / demo build. Only merged from `develop`. Never direct commits.   |
| `develop`               | Integration branch. All completed work lands here first.                   |
| `feature/<description>` | New functionality, branched from and merged into `develop`.               |
| `bugfix/<description>`  | Defect fix on `develop`, branched from and merged into `develop`.         |
| `hotfix/<description>`  | Urgent fix branched from `main`, merged into both `main` and `develop`.   |

**These are the only branch prefixes.** Conventional Commits types such as `chore`, `docs`, `ci` and
`refactor` are **commit-message types, not branch prefixes** — they never appear in a branch name. A
documentation change lives on a `feature/*` branch and carries `docs:` commits.

**Branch name examples:**
```
feature/gemma-inference-service
feature/rag-recipe-retrieval
feature/iron-coverage-calculation
bugfix/plan-screen-null-hemoglobin
```

## Commit Convention

We follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/):

```
<type>(<scope>): <short description in lowercase>
```

| Type       | When to use                                             |
|------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
| `feat`     | New feature or capability                               |
| `fix`      | Bug fix                                                 |
| `refactor` | Code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature |
| `test`     | Adding or fixing tests                                  |
| `docs`     | Documentation only (README, CHANGELOG, docs/, ADRs)     |
| `build`    | Build system or dependencies (`pubspec.yaml`, Gradle)   |
| `ci`       | CI/CD configuration (GitHub Actions, Lefthook)          |
| `chore`    | Maintenance, config, `.gitignore`                       |
| `style`    | Formatting only (no logic change)                       |
| `perf`     | Performance improvement                                 |

**Scope** = the area you touched: `inference`, `rag`, `nutrition`, `storage`, `onboarding`, `home`,
`plan`, `ci`, `docs`.

**Examples:**
```
feat(plan): add iron coverage calculation
feat(inference): wire flutter_gemma behind InferenceService
fix(onboarding): allow saving a profile without a hemoglobin reading
docs(adr): record gitflow branching model
```

### Atomic commits

**One logical change per commit.** A commit that bundles unrelated work cannot be reviewed and
cannot be reverted without unpicking things that were fine. If the description needs an "and", it is
two commits.

```bash
git add lib/core/nutrition/iron_requirements.dart
git commit -m "feat(nutrition): add age-band iron requirement table"

git add test/core/nutrition/iron_requirements_test.dart
git commit -m "test(nutrition): cover iron requirement table per age band"
```

## Workflow

```
1. Branch from develop
   git checkout develop && git pull origin develop
   git checkout -b feature/my-feature

2. Implement, keeping the build green
   dart format . && flutter analyze && flutter test

3. Commit atomically, following the convention
   git add <files>
   git commit -m "feat(scope): description"

4. Update CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased]

5. Push and open a Pull Request targeting develop
   git push origin feature/my-feature
```

During the first hours everyone works against mocks so nobody blocks anybody: UI runs on
`FakeInferenceService`, RAG runs on a five-recipe sample corpus, inference is validated standalone on
a real handset, and storage is filled with seeds. Real integration happens at the **hour-4
checkpoint**, not before.

## Pull Requests

- Every PR targets `develop`, never `main` directly.
- CI (`format` + `analyze` + `test`) must pass. **A red CI is the merge gate.**
- CODEOWNERS notifies the area owner but **does not block the merge** — blocking would stall four
  developers who are all coding at once. Review is expected; waiting is not.
- Fill out the [PR template](./PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md) honestly.
- Keep PRs scoped to one area. A PR touching `inference` and `plan` and `storage` is three PRs.
- State which device you verified on. "Works on the iOS Simulator" is not verification for anything
  touching inference.

## Updating the CHANGELOG

Add your change under `## [Unreleased]` in [`CHANGELOG.md`](../CHANGELOG.md) following
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/):

```markdown
## [Unreleased]
### Added
- nutrition: iron coverage calculation against age-band requirements
### Fixed
- onboarding: profile could not be saved without a hemoglobin reading
```
